tweets.text:
Good assessment of the on the ground reality for security in most large enterprises right now. The fragmented landscape of the risk surface is only going to get more gnarly, making it even more complex for enterprises to solve.

There’s a never ending set of libraries to keep up with, tools to leverage, and sprawling infrastructure, data, and code to secure. Most large enterprises can barely keep up with this, let alone smaller startups or most companies outside of tech. 

In many cases enterprises need to work to modernize their tech stacks. Data, in most organizations, is highly fragmented which means you don’t really know the state of risk at any given time. Some systems are open up privileges too broadly, and others are operating primarily via security through obscurity. Lots of upgrading here to do.

Once you can get your data and infra into a better spot, at least you have a chance for agents to help you secure the environment. Agent swarms can fan out, leverage any security tool, test various perpetuations of attacks, read through logs, process enterprise data for risk level, and more. This capability only emerged in the past few months, and none of it would be possible before we had long running agents and computer use good enough.

This is a huge area of opportunity right now for every layer of the security stack across identity, firewall, network, code scanning, data protection, and more. And it’s at least one reason to be optimistic about the balance of offensive and defensive capability. 

But everyone does need to do the hard work of getting the basics right at the start.

tweets.text:
the bear case for AI is here, some observations why (h/t chamath):

- the moneys fake: 80% of revenue in AI comes from VC subsidised companies.

- neoclouds are incredibly disorganised and lack ability to deliver on their contracts. this will result in an implosion in 2027. 

- hyperscalers are losing money on billions of dollars worth of gpus collecting dust because they can’t power them. anthropic s-1 rumored to prove this (releasing tmr i think)

- there’s no more money in the debt market to lend to scalers. investment-grade loans require independent lines of revenue generation and 200+ neoclouds will fail this.

bonus: insurance market is scrambling to support $1-5M penalties charged by labs / hyperscalers to data center builders who’ve fallen behind on delivery times. 

2027 is going to be bumpy. period of up-only is over for a bit.

every shopping platform will need to embrace AI in the same way Walmart is - this is the case study to watch:

-  amazon banned ai agents from shopping, walmart did the opposite - any agent (muse, gemini, GPT) gets its own account, can browse and shop on behalf of a human 

- browsing history, shopping preferences are kept private to the user. 

- human can set spending limits and view, return any items the agent buys. great shopping experience, less pressure on “risk”

on average every meta muse user is spending $200, i expect this to dramatically increase as more of the world replaces browsers with personal ai agents

whoever owns the agent platform will take % fee on all transactions and make an absolute killing

hot take: ai models aren’t suited for humans, they’re suited for agents, think about it:

- to date the most effective AI products leverage swarms or 100s of persistent agents talking to each other. grok bot, muse etc all do this too.

- 99% humans don’t really know what to do with a model, an agent built on your context tho? does.

this isn’t me saying humans aren’t in the equation, they’re just at a higher abstraction (talking to personal agents)

assume every human has multiple agents running 24/7 talking to one another 

that’s the future to expect

tweets.text:
🚨「特朗普内幕巨鲸」再度重仓做空，比特币要迎来新一轮暴跌？

据 @CryptoNobler 曝光的 Hyperdash 仓位截图，一名被市场称为「特朗普内幕人士」的交易者，在美国期货市场开盘前建立了约 1.81 亿美元的 BTC 空头头寸，杠杆约 13 倍。

这名交易者此前多次因精准押中市场大跌而受到关注，社交媒体甚至将其描述为「100% 胜率」。如今再度重仓做空，市场难免猜测：他是否又在押注某个尚未公开的重大消息？

值得注意的是，这类传闻并非第一次出现。2025 年 10 月特朗普宣布对中国商品加征 100% 关税前，一名通过 Hyperliquid 建立大额 BTC、ETH 空头的交易者曾因交易时机引发广泛讨论，相关报道估算其获利约 1.6 亿至 2 亿美元。但其是否掌握内幕信息，始终缺乏确凿证据。

这次真正值得追踪的，不是他是否「知道消息」，而是这笔 1.81 亿美元空头会如何变化，以及市场是否出现与之呼应的资金和价格信号。

巨鲸可以押注崩盘，但不能替市场宣布崩盘。

昨天刚走一个，今天又双叒走一个！Anthropic 快 IPO 了，核心人才却接连离场。

昨天，Claude Code 核心工程师 Thariq Shihipar 宣布离职；今天，Claude Code 桌面版创建者 Anthony Morris 也宣布离开。

两人连续出走，未必意味着 Anthropic 内部出了问题，但这个时间点值得琢磨。

IPO 前夕，Anthropic 正从高速增长的 AI 创业公司，转向一家需要对估值、营收和长期盈利能力负责的巨头。

对早期核心员工而言，这可能也是职业选择的分水岭：

一边是继续留在公司，等待 IPO 带来的股权兑现；另一边是趁 AI Agent 创业窗口仍然打开，带着技术积累和行业声望重新下注。

尤其是 Claude Code，已经证明了 AI 编程工具的商业价值。亲手参与产品从 0 到 1 的人，未必愿意一直做大公司里的螺丝钉。

当然，目前没有证据表明两人的离职与 IPO 直接相关，具体去向也尚未明确。

但一个值得关注的信号是：当 AI 巨头开始冲刺上市，下一波 AI 创业公司的创始人，可能正从这些巨头的核心团队里走出来。

Anthropic 在为 IPO 做准备，硅谷的人才流动也可能在为下一轮创业周期做准备。

🚨 Arthur Hayes 持续清仓中！

BitMEX 联合创始人 Arthur Hayes (@CryptoHayes) 近期频繁进行链上操作，目前已正式执行其“离场观望”策略：

累计向各大交易平台转入价值 2,881 万美元 的多种代币（涉及 ETH、ENA、UNI、ETHFI、AERO、PENDLE、ZAMA 等）

已陆续从交易所提回 1,415 万枚 USDC

他认为当前宏观经济与地缘政治存在不确定性，市场可能需要经历下跌才能重新上涨，决定暂时离场等待风险解除的明确信号。

Shaw 此前刚完成对 https://t.co/f597vUlytv合约的字节级逆向，并在主网程序中发现一个关键安全漏洞。这次他把同样的方法应用到了 https://t.co/iTQE8daAmX。他公开的 GitHub 仓库 lalalune/pumpfun-source 显示，目前已捕获 Pump、PumpSwap、Pump Fees 和 Mayhem 等程序的完整部署证据，并正在尝试进行字节精确的源码重建。仓库本身明确标注“incomplete”（未完成），目前还没有完整可部署的重构程序。

这件事在社区引发了两极反应：
一部分人认为这是对透明度的推动，有助于发现漏洞、降低系统性风险；
另一部分人则担心，把热门协议的完整逻辑摊开，会降低攻击门槛，尤其是在 memecoin 和 bonding curve 这类高投机场景下。

Shaw 的立场表明：与其继续靠不公开源码维持护城河，不如把逻辑摊开，让风险在明面上被检验。

I am okay with Kimi 3.1 deliberately leaving out top-end offensive cyber capabilities from their training data.

Discriminating against use cases is MUCH less bad than discriminating against users. And the world does need all the time it can get to prepare, harden, check old code, (properly) formally verify new code, etc before the full weight of very powerful cyber attacks is upon us.

And if this first big wave of AI risk is not handled well, then we may well get a dystopia of highly locked down models, KYC gating on everything, highly intrusive surveillance on everything, a society where you may be a second or third or fourth-class citizen in terms of model access based on your credentials and nationality.
